cards.label: ACT
cards.claim: A causal test can show whether a network's global workspace actually does the computing or only relays answers computed elsewhere, which task accuracy and ablation tests cannot distinguish.
cards.people: Diaoxuan He, Linqian Wu (affiliations not in source)
cards.stage_headline: Stage 3 of 5: tested against a control.
cards.stage_note: The test was checked against networks deliberately built either to relay or to recombine information, a known-answer control, and the abstract says it identified the computation correctly in every case. No other team has repeated it. Read from the arXiv listing abstract only.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: It turns a central claim of Global Workspace Theory (information becomes conscious when it is broadcast to specialised processes that then use it) into a property that can be tested in trained models. That matters for claims about consciousness in AI.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: On networks built to be either relays or recombiners, the causal test recovered the correct answer in every case, while accuracy and ablation could not tell them apart.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: How well it works on large pretrained models. The abstract mentions only one known interface in a pretrained Transformer. Whether code is released is also unknown.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: Released code, and an independent team applying it to a different model family.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: Built-in relay-or-recombine networks that the test misclassifies.

cards.todo: Read the paper this week and check whether code is released.
cards.rule_text: If the code is open, consider it for a small methods grant to test it independently.
cards.compare_text: Read against the adversarial collaborative review of integrated information and predictive processing theories.

cards.label: WATCH
cards.claim: Axion quark nuggets, a proposed form of dark matter, could explain reported UAP features: high speed, extreme acceleration, no leftover material and no sonic boom despite supersonic motion.
cards.stage_headline: Stage 1 of 5: an idea, not yet tested.
cards.stage_note: It's a theoretical argument. The abstract cites no UAP dataset or comparison group.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: It would link UAP to dark matter physics. The author says he uses the same parameters as his earlier AQN work, which limits how much the model can be tuned. He has previously used AQN to explain other anomalies, such as the ANITA events (arXiv:2105.01668).

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: It argues that some UAP belong with sky-quakes, ball lightning and other unexplained transient events, all driven by the nugget's antiquark core.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Which specific UAP events are modelled, if any; whether it makes numerical predictions for brightness, sound or radiation; how it fits existing AQN constraints. No critiques found.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: A testable prediction, such as a radiation or acoustic signature, compared against UAP records with sensor data (Galileo Project, or AARO cases with official analysis).

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: Well-instrumented supersonic UAP with no matching signature, or the AQN parameter range being ruled out by other dark matter searches.

cards.rule_text: A follow-up that compares the model with a sensor-instrumented UAP dataset.
cards.compare_text: Galileo Project's first triangulation results (Avi Loeb's blog, about 8 weeks old).

primary_link.label: arXiv: axion quark nuggets and UAP ↗

cards.label: WATCH
cards.claim: An exoplanet's ionospheric radio cutoff should rise and fall over its orbit, which could mark broadband radio leakage as coming from the planet and also probe exoplanet ionospheres.
cards.people: Michael A. Garrett (University of Manchester; Leiden Observatory and University of Malta also listed)
cards.stage_headline: Stage 1 of 5: an idea, not yet tested.
cards.stage_note: It's a model with no observations. The author calls detection observationally challenging.
cards.impact_heading: IF TRUE, HOW BIG A DEAL?
cards.impact_text: It gives a physical check that separates a planet's own radio leakage from local interference on Earth.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: Oblique propagation, magnetic fields and absorption smooth the cutoff into a gradual escape function. Delays in the atmosphere's response shift its timing a little, but the rise and fall survives.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Whether current instruments could detect it.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: Detectability forecasts for instruments such as LOFAR or SKA-Low on real target lists.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong (as a useful test)
details.text: A finding that for all realistic targets the cutoff falls below the frequency at which ground-based telescopes can see through Earth's own ionosphere.

cards.rule_text: A detectability forecast or a pilot analysis on low-frequency radio data.
cards.compare_text: Garrett's earlier framework for broadband radio leakage, MNRAS 549(3) stag991.

cards.label: CRITIQUE
cards.claim: The Visual Awareness Negativity changes reliably with attention, which challenges its use as a specific marker of conscious perception.
cards.people: Łucja Doradzińska, Michał Bola (affiliations not in source)
cards.stage_headline: Stage 3 of 5: tested against a control.
cards.stage_note: Attention was manipulated experimentally, and a second experiment confirmed the effect. Preregistration status not seen; the PDF was not opened.
cards.impact_text: The VAN, a brain-wave signal about 200–300 ms after a stimulus, is widely used as a marker of consciousness. If it tracks attention, that marker is weakened.

details.heading: What they say
details.text: VAN amplitude changes reliably with attention, confirmed in Experiment 2.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: Sample sizes, effect sizes, and whether a VAN remains once attention is controlled.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: A preregistered study where awareness and attention vary independently and the VAN tracks awareness only.

cards.todo: Read the full text before funding any VAN-based consciousness work.
cards.rule_text: Hold any VAN-based funding decision until the full text has been read.

cards.label: CRITIQUE
cards.meta: SPECULATIVE GRAVITY · ARXIV COMMENT PAPER (GR-QC) · NOV 17
cards.claim: The black hole solution proposed in arXiv:2511.14047 fails the field equations of general relativity with a DBI scalar near the horizon, so it is not a black hole in that theory.
cards.people: Mustapha Azreg-Aïnou, Marco A. A. de Paula (affiliations not in source)
cards.stage_note: A consistency check on a theoretical solution, so the evidence scale doesn't apply. Read from the arXiv listing abstract only.
cards.impact_text: Low stakes for our remit, which touches primordial dark matter, but it is a clean example of a comment paper correcting a published solution.

details.heading: What they say
details.text: The physical branch of the DBI field ends outside the event horizon, so the solution does not satisfy all field equations there.

details.heading: Keep in mind
details.text: No reply from the original authors has been seen. A reply or correction would settle it.

cards.rule_text: A reply from the original authors, or a correction to arXiv:2511.14047.
cards.compare_text: Read against the original paper, arXiv:2511.14047.

cards.label: CONTEXT
cards.meta: RESEARCH INTEGRITY · RETRACTION WATCH NEWS · NOV 19
cards.claim: Hidden instructions to AI reviewers are turning up inside preprints and published papers.
cards.people: Reported by Retraction Watch; found by sleuth Nick Brown
cards.stage_note: A news report, not a new claim.
cards.impact_text: If we use AI tools to help triage grantee preprints, hidden prompts could bias that triage.

details.heading: What happened
details.text: Nick Brown found hidden text asking AI reviewers to give a paper a good review, placed in a figure in a font coloured to match the graph. Such prompts are now appearing in published papers.

details.heading: Keep in mind
details.text: None of the reported cases were in our topic areas.

cards.todo: Add a hidden-text and prompt-injection check to how we screen grantee preprints, especially where AI tools help with triage.

cards.label: BENCHMARK
cards.meta: ZERO-POINT AND VACUUM PHYSICS · ARXIV PREPRINT (QUANT-PH) · NOV 19
cards.claim: A precise measurement of the magnetic field reflected from a copper plate disagrees with both the Drude and plasma models of metals, and its phase, measured for the first time, disagrees qualitatively with Drude.
cards.people: M. Dhital, G. L. Klimchitskaya, V. M. Mostepanenko, U. Mohideen (affiliations not in source)
cards.stage_headline: Stage 2 of 5: uses data, but no comparison group.
cards.stage_note: One team's measurement compared with theory; no independent repeat known. Checked through search excerpts of the full text only.
cards.impact_text: It probes the s-polarised evanescent waves at the centre of the Casimir puzzle, where force measurements fit the plasma model rather than the physically expected Drude model. The baseline theory of vacuum forces near metals is itself unsettled, and any zero-point energy device must be judged against it.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: According to the paper, the plasma model disagrees with this data even more strongly than the Drude model does, so neither explains it.

details.heading: Still unknown
details.text: The size of the discrepancy in standard-deviation terms, and the error budget.

details.heading: Would make it more convincing
details.text: An independent group repeating the magnitude and phase measurement.

details.heading: Would prove it wrong
details.text: An independent measurement that agrees with the Drude model.

cards.todo: Read it and use it as the reference standard for any zero-point energy proposal.
cards.rule_text: If an independent lab offers to repeat the measurement, scoping a replication is in remit.
cards.compare_text: The same group's earlier paper, 'Casimir effect invalidates the Drude model for TE evanescent waves'.

primary_link.label: arXiv: reflected magnetic field from copper and the Casimir puzzle ↗

cards.label: BENCHMARK
cards.claim: Simons Observatory and CMB-S4 on their own cannot distinguish DESI's preferred evolving dark energy from a cosmological-constant model that mimics the same CMB pattern; ΛCDM stays within about 2σ.
cards.people: Anna Chiara Ferri, Ruchika, Alessandro Melchiorri (affiliations not in source)
cards.stage_note: A forecast, not a measurement, so the evidence scale doesn't apply. Checked through search excerpts of the full text.
cards.impact_text: This week's dynamic vacuum energy papers in physics.gen-ph rest on the DESI DR2 dark energy hint. CMB data alone won't confirm it, so the evidence still depends on DESI and supernova data.

details.heading: What the work shows
details.text: Next-generation CMB experiments alone leave ΛCDM within about 2σ of the DESI-preferred evolving dark energy.

details.heading: Keep in mind
details.text: It is a forecast; conclusions depend on the simulated data assumptions.

cards.todo: No action. Keep it as the reference point for vacuum-decay claims.
cards.compare_text: Read the physics.gen-ph dynamic vacuum energy papers (Millo 2611.23449; Chaudhary et al. 2611.23340) against this forecast.
